[[California's 22nd congressional district]] became vacant when [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] representative [[Devin Nunes]] resigned on January 1, 2022, to become the CEO of the [[Trump Media & Technology Group]].{{cite web|last=Korte|first=Lara|date=December 6, 2021|title=Devin Nunes' retirement could mean an opening for California Democrats. Who might run?|url=https://www.sacbee.com/news/politics-government/capitol-alert/article256384562.html|access-date=December 6, 2021|website=Sacramento Bee}} [[Governor of California|Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] scheduled the special election for June 7, 2022, with the primary election on April 5, 2022.{{Cite web|last=Brassil|first=Gillian|date=January 9, 2022|title=These 5 candidates want a shot at Devin Nunes' seat, even if it lasts only 6 months|url=https://www.fresnobee.com/news/politics-government/article257147057.html|access-date=January 9, 2022|website=www.fresnobee.com|publisher=[[The Fresno Bee]]|language=en-US}} The election was held using a [[nonpartisan blanket primary]], a system where all candidates run in the same primary, and if no candidate receives a majority of votes, the top two candidates then advance to the general election.{{Cite web|title=Elections Code Division 10 Part 6 Chapter 1|url=https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=ELEC&division=10.&title=&part=6.&chapter=1.&article=|url-status=live|website=California Legislative Information|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150709231709/https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=ELEC&division=10.&title=&part=6.&chapter=1.&article= |archive-date=July 9, 2015 }} No candidate received a majority in the primary, so Republican [[Connie Conway]] and Democrat Lourin Hubbard advanced to the runoff. ==Nonpartisan blanket primary==
